metadata.description: Compare IPFlex static residential, dynamic residential, and datacenter proxies by use case, protocol support, operational fit, and decision criteria so teams can choose the right proxy type with less guesswork.

slogan.line1: Short answer: use static residential proxies for persistent sessions, dynamic residential proxies for broad coverage, and datacenter proxies for throughput-cost efficiency.
slogan.line2: This page helps teams compare proxy types by workload fit, operating limits, and rollout guidance.

staticResidential.title: Static Residential Proxy
staticResidential.description: A proxy service based on real residential networks, providing fixed IP addresses that remain unchanged for long periods. It features high anonymity and credibility, effectively avoiding proxy detection or blocking, suitable for various business scenarios such as cross-border e-commerce, market research, social media marketing, and brand protection.

dynamicResidential.title: Dynamic Residential Proxy
dynamicResidential.description: A proxy service based on a constantly changing IP address pool, providing frequently rotating IP addresses in short periods. This service offers high flexibility and extensive IP coverage, effectively bypassing IP bans and restrictions, suitable for scenarios requiring frequent IP changes such as web scraping, data collection, ad verification, and automated testing.

datacenter.title: Datacenter Proxy
datacenter.description: A proxy service based on datacenter networks, providing fixed IP addresses that remain unchanged for long periods. This proxy service delivers IPs through datacenter servers, typically offering higher speed and stability, with advantages in cost and performance, particularly suitable for scenarios requiring fast, large-scale data collection and access, such as website testing, data analysis, SEO monitoring, and online ad verification.
